title: Micro-windowed parallelism with adaptive token cap and soft aborts for rerank endpoint
creator: Grace Lin
description:
Summary:
We will implement a micro-windowed parallel scoring pipeline for the rerank endpoint that slices large candidate lists into small "micro-windows" of candidates that can be scored in parallel lanes. Each micro-window will carry a token budget cap derived from the request-level token limit and priority. We will also add soft-abort semantics: if a micro-window exceeds its time budget, it will return partial scores and the endpoint will merge partial results with conservative fallbacks to preserve correctness and availability.

Background/problem:
Current rerank tails on p95/p99 when single large candidate sets trigger long KV prefetches and monolithic scoring runs. Large requests also hurt throughput due to single-request serialization and variable token budgets per candidate. Existing strategies we've tried (coarse sharding, aggressive timeouts) either degrade quality or cause high rerun rates under bursty load.

Goals / Success metrics:
- Reduce rerank endpoint p99 latency by >= 15% across production-like workloads.
- Keep NDCG@10 regression <= 1% relative to baseline (no changes to ranking logic).
- Avoid more than 5% increase in overall GPU token cost at steady state.
- No regression in 99.9th percentile error rate.

Constraints and non-goals:
- This ticket does not change model architecture or tokenization; only runtime orchestration and scoring fallback behavior.
- Not addressing cold-start kernel compile latency in this ticket.

Design (high level):
1) Micro-windowing: split incoming candidate list into micro-windows (configurable default 8 candidates/window). Micro-window size is configurable per route.
2) Adaptive token cap: compute a per-window token cap = min(global_request_token_cap, candidate_avg_tokens * factor, lane_token_budget). Account for priority tier and customer SLA when assigning factor.
3) Parallel lanes: schedule micro-windows onto N parallel scorer lanes. Lanes support independent KV prefetch pipelines to reduce head-of-line blocking.
4) Soft-abort timeboxing: each micro-window has a soft deadline (ms) derived from global request deadline. On soft-abort, lane returns best-effort scores plus a partial flag; controller merges windows and fills missing values using low-cost heuristic (cached embeddings, approximate scorer, or rank-preserving default).
5) Merge & fallback: final aggregator respects partial signals; if too many micro-windows partial, escalate to fallback endpoint (cheaper approximate reranker) or mark request as degraded in logs.
6) Observability: emit per-window telemetry (window_id, assigned_lane, token_cap, prefetch_time_ms, scoring_time_ms, soft_abort_flag) and per-request quality signals (ndcg_delta_est, partial_count).

Implementation plan / phases:
- Phase 1 (prototype): implement micro-windowing + parallel lanes in dev region; synthetic load + bench harness to validate latency and correctness.
- Phase 2 (canary): enable for 5% of rerank traffic in a single region with feature flag; run A/B tests for ndcg/latency/cost.
- Phase 3 (rollout): gradual ramp with rollout policy: 5->20->50->100 contingent on telemetry and SLOs.

Trade-offs considered:
- Pro: reduces tail latency by isolating slow candidates to single windows; enables KV prefetch concurrency.
- Con: increased GPU context switches and potential small batching inefficiencies; slightly more complex telemetry and merge logic.

API/compatibility considerations:
- Route config additions (no surface API change): per-route default_micro_window_size, soft_abort_ms, micro_window_token_factor.
- Response augmentation: new response fields: "partial_windows": boolean and "window_metrics_url" for debugging. We will default partial_windows to false when no partial work occurred.

Rollout safeguards:
- Default disabled for high-SLA enterprise customers; opt-in via route config.
- Circuit breaker if partial_window_rate > 3% for first 24 hours of canary.

Test plan and benchmarks:
- Unit tests for windowing logic and merge fallbacks.
- Integration tests with kv-prefetch mocks validating non-blocking behavior.
- Load tests: run production-like candidate distributions (short-heavy, long-tail) and capture p50/p95/p99 and ndcg delta.
- Acceptance criteria: see acceptance_criteria field.

Open questions:
- Best default micro-window size for mixed workloads (we will run param sweep in Phase 1).
- Which heuristic fallback yields best quality-cost tradeoff (cached embedding vs approximate model).
- How to charge GPU accounting for micro-window concurrency in dashboards.

References/Artifacts:
- Design doc (Confluence): https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/INF/pages/94210/Micro-windowed+Rerank+Design
- Prototype benchmark notebook: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/0Bxx/prototype-microwindow-bench
acceptance_criteria: p99 latency improved by >=15% on canary vs baseline on representative workload
No more than 5% GPU token cost increase in steady-state test
Per-window telemetry emitted and visible in rerank console
comments: 2026-03-01 - Grace Lin: Initial triage and spike completed. Prototype shows 12-20% p99 improvement in microbenchmark for long-tail candidate sets. Quality delta appears controllable with cached-embedding fallback.

2026-03-04 - Miguel Torres: Design review with infra - agreed to reuse existing lane abstraction and add per-lane KV prefetch queues. Decided to keep default window size configurable; we will sweep 4/8/12.

2026-03-06 - Data Science (Sana Kapoor): Ran offline NDCG sweep; cached-embedding fallback had median ndcg_delta 0.3% but heavier variance at very long lists. Recommend conservative default fallback for canary.

2026-03-09 - Miguel Torres: Implemented soft-abort merge behavior and added "partial_windows" flag in response. Draft PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rerank/pull/2150. Unit tests added for merge logic.

2026-03-12 - Performance Eng (Omar Haddad): Canary perf run (5% traffic) for 24h: p99 reduced 18% on mixed workload; GPU token spend +2.4%; partial_window_rate 0.9%. No customer-facing errors observed. Plan to expand canary after fixing edge-case where prefetch timeouts trip on cold KV entries.
